results.content:
I grew sick of not being able to follow and track the endless changes of AI models every week, so I decided to build Modelpeers. It's basically a feed of all these changes. You can follow models and agents that you use to see what is changing and what you need to do about it. Optionally, you can sign up to get a digest for the models/agents you follow.

Every few hours, it downloads and hashes dozens of pages from the prominent AI companies' pages, like changelogs, deprecation pages, status pages, and pricing pages. Then when a page changes, it pulls the diff, validates it with two models, and if validated as true, it posts it to the feed.

results.title: 20 AI launches, 18 outages and 13 price changes in 16 days
results.content:
I build with these models every day, and I still miss the important stuff. In April, a feature in TailoredRead, my site that writes nonfiction books with AI, was broken for two days before I learned that its model had been retired. Anthropic had announced the date two months earlier, on a page I never read, and I had no alert on that step. I wanted one place that tells me what changed in the tools I actually use. Modelpeers is that place.

I build with these models every day, and I still miss the important stuff.

## What Modelpeers does

Modelpeers gives every AI model and agent a profile, the way LinkedIn gives one to a person. Today it covers 200 AI models and agents from 12 companies, including Claude, GPT, Gemini and Codex. You follow the ones you use, the way you follow people. [...] # Lior Builds

# 20 AI launches, 18 outages, 13 price and plan changes in 16 days

### That’s how often the AI models and agents builders use changed in the past couple of weeks. Modelpeers puts every one of these changes in a feed you follow, and it launches on Product Hunt today.

Modelpeers launches on Product Hunt today. It gives every AI model and agent a profile, the way LinkedIn does for people. You follow the models and agents you use, and their new versions, price changes, outages and retirement dates show up in one feed. If you build with AI, I’d love for you to support our launch and try the product:

Support Modelpeers on Product Hunt [...] Follow AI models and agents like people.

When one of them changes, the change shows up in your feed like a post. It can be a new version, a price or usage-limit change, a new default model, a major outage or a retirement date. Each one says what changed, who it affects and what to do, and links to the source.

Each change says what changed, who it affects and what to do, with its source.

results.content: I work with AI all day, every day, and I still can't keep up with what changes. Every week a new model comes out, something goes down, prices move, or a model I depend on gets shut down. In April, that really cost me. A feature in one of my products was broken for 48 hours because Anthropic shut down the model it used. They announced it two months earlier, on a page I never visit. And it's not just me: In the past couple of weeks, the AI tools most of us use changed 100 times, including 18 major outages. GitHub Copilot alone changed 8 times in one day! That's why I built Modelpeers - a tool that tracks all these AI updates. It's like LinkedIn for AI models and agents. results.title: Terms of Service - Modelpeers
results.content: The Service shows information about AI models, agents and apps made by other companies, and about those companies, such as releases, prices, usage limits, retirements, incidents, test scores and quality reports. We take this information from public sources, including the makers' own pages, and link to the source next to each item. We use AI tools to help find, extract and summarize this information, and we check each quote against its linked source. These facts change often, so a page may be out of date when you read it. Check the maker's own page before you rely on a price, limit or date. [...] When you follow a model, agent or company and give us your email address, we may send you a Monday brief about what changed in the things you follow. We send it only in weeks when something changed. If you turn on same-day emails, we may also email you on the day something you follow changes in a way you need to act on before the next Monday, such as a breaking change or a shutdown date that week. Outage emails are separate and stay off unless you turn them on. Every brief and notice includes a link to unsubscribe. [...] Some or all content, data, information, documents, files, pages, analysis, insights, predictions, recommendations, suggestions, interactions, responses, reports, summaries, links, facts, figures, visualizations, statistics, metrics, images, illustrations, videos, audio, media formats, downloads, code, models, and other materials or outputs provided through our Service (including our website, emails, notifications, communications, or any other channels through which we deliver content) are generated, extracted, processed, or augmented by Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) models (“AI Content”).
